import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 45

Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$,
such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least 10 of them?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
- [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»`.
-/

findings.description: The claimed canonical redirect supplies only the twofold variant, not Green's tenfold question. This file contains no declarations of its own and imports Erdos689.erdos_689, whose coverage requirement is `2 ≤ (...).card`. There is no tenfold statement in the imported problem file. Thus the redirect substitutes the weaker question mentioned in Green's comments for the main question reproduced in this file. Tenfold coverage implies twofold coverage, but the twofold requirement does not impose Green's bound of ten. Erdos689.erdos_689 itself correctly states the Erdős website's twofold question; the issue is presenting it as the canonical formalization of Green 45.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 Open Problems, Problem 45, p. 23, asks whether every integer up to N can lie in 'at least 10' chosen residue classes. Its comments explicitly distinguish the other case: 'Erdős remarks that he does not know how to answer it with 10 replaced by 2.' https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45. The Erdős #689 page states the twofold question and describes other fixed multiplicities as similar questions: https://erdosproblems.com/689.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a tenfold declaration in this file, or add a tenfold variant to the canonical Erdős file and point specifically to that variant. Its statement should be `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, 10 ≤ ((Finset.Icc 1 n).filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card`. Retain the existing twofold Erdős declaration as a separate variant.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf — introduction/notation, Problem 45 and comments, bibliography entry [109]
https://erdosproblems.com/689 — statement, variants and OPEN status, read through https://r.jina.ai/https://erdosproblems.com/689
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf — P. Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory, §6, Problem 6, p. 108
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliographic identification of the primary paper
review.notes: The target is an import-only pointer, so the finding is file-level, not an error in the imported theorem considered against its own twofold source. The imported theorem's quantifier order, answer scope, natural-number residue representatives, prime filtering, interval endpoints and eventual quantification check out. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/statement-comparison.lean compile successfully; checks include empty and smallest intervals, representative normalization, exclusion of 1 from the prime count, and the tenfold-to-twofold implication. No converse equivalence was established. The Erdős page still records the problem as OPEN, matching the imported category.

not_demonstrated.reason: The target contains no declarations; the reported issue concerns its redirect to Erdos689.erdos_689, which faithfully states the genuinely open twofold covering question. Neither a short proof nor a short refutation is available. Proving tenfold coverage implies twofold coverage, or checking isolated finite inputs, would not demonstrate a defect in the quantified statement.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created; /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean is absent.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported mismatch concerns which conjecture the import-only file supplies, not a declaration made trivially true or false. An honest proof or disproof of the imported statement would require resolving the actual twofold covering problem.

submission.summary: Added the tenfold covering question for all sufficiently large N, with the appropriate answer placeholder, docstring, and category/AMS attributes. Clarified that the imported Erdős theorem states the weaker twofold variant and left it unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the permitted `sorry` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 45

Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$,
such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least 10 of them?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 45](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.45)
- [erdosproblems.com/689](https://www.erdosproblems.com/689)

The weaker version requiring coverage by at least two classes is formalized in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«689»`.
-/

namespace Green45

/--
For all sufficiently large $N$, can we choose a residue class modulo each prime $p \leq N$
so that every integer in $[1, N]$ lies in at least ten of these classes?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_45 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      10 ≤ ((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter fun p => p.Prime ∧ a p ≡ m [MOD p]).card := by
  sorry

end Green45
